label: Opening-bigram detector: first token o, or a specific first-two-token pair (first in {i,a,x,f,n,d,m}, second in {o,a,n,l,i,f,p,m})
explanation: Fires only in the first three steps of the original phase (t=0..2); never at the delimiter or during copy. At t=0 it fires on every sequence starting with o, weakly (~0.14 of max). Most mass (~81%) is at t=1, where it depends on the pair (first token, second token): first token from {i,a,x,f,n,d,m} and second from {o,a,n,l,i,f,p,m}. The strongest pair is i followed by o (activation = max); o as the second token is strongest overall. If the sequence starts with o, the t=1 step does NOT fire. Residual misses are weaker t=2 activations with similar token combinations (e.g. i x i, r m o, f d a) and weak t=1 hits after r or s. It does not fire on b, and only rarely on d, s or r as the current token.

issues: Scope mismatch with the user's request: the user asked for the baseline to be run on the subsampled data in features/copy_transcoder_v2_1of5. All of this checking, including the original agent's, used features/copy_gru_v1_neuron_baseline_store. Nothing shows that store was built from the 1/5 subsample, so these results may not be the run the user asked for.

The reported test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.978, R 0.732, F1 0.837, mass recall 0.852). The basic claims also hold: the unit fires only at t=0..2, never at the delimiter or in the copy phase; t=0 & o has precision 1.0; about 81% of activation mass is at t=1; there is no activation on b; and t=1 after an initial o is nearly silent (precision 0.033).

Systematic miss class 1, t=1 after a first token of r or s: (t==1) & prev_tok in {r,s} & in_tok in B has precision 0.62 and covers 8.5% of actives. The explanation calls these 'weak t=1 hits after r or s' and treats them as noise, but the label and predicate then define the first-token set as excluding r and s. So the set is not a clean boundary.

Systematic miss class 2, t=2 when all three opening tokens fit the pattern: (t==2) & prev2_tok in A & prev_tok in A & in_tok in B has precision 0.66. These t=2 hits can be strong (for example i,i,r at 0.88 and n,f,l at 0.53). They are not just 'weaker t=2 activations'.
Weaker class: t=1 with the first token in A and r or s as the second token has precision 0.36.

The label overclaims sharpness. Calling it an 'opening-bigram detector' with fixed sets reads like a crisp lookup table. The data look more graded: an evidence score that builds up over the first 1-3 tokens, with the A/B sets as approximations and r/s at the edge. Also, t=1 & in_tok==o alone has precision of only 0.39, so 'o as second token is the strongest' holds only when the first token is in A.
skeptic.revised_label: Opening-token-pattern unit, fires only at t=0..2. It fires on an initial o, and mostly at t=1 when the first token is in {i,a,x,f,n,d,m} (more weakly r or s) and the second is in {o,a,n,l,i,f,p,m}. It continues at t=2 when the first two tokens are both from the first-token set and the third is in the second-token set.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=0: o; t=1: o, l, n, a; t=2: o, a, n, i) and the previous input (most: i, a, x, f, d, n; least: j, 3, q, y); timing cues that raise it most: t=1, t=0, t=2.
